chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who stole, so he said: I heard my father saying: A man who had stolen was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) during his time, so he cut his hand. Then he was brought to him a second time, so he cut his leg from the opposite side. Then he was brought to him a third time, so he kept him imprisoned for life and spent upon him from the treasury of the Muslims, and said: This is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do. I will not oppose him.

key_terms.رِجْلَهُ مِنْ خِلَافٍ: his leg from the opposite side

ai.seo_question: What is the progressive punishment for repeated theft according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential precedent for the progressive punishment of theft, linking the practice of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) directly to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). It highlights a distinct Shia interpretation where the third offense results in lifelong imprisonment and financial support from the bayt al-mal, rather than a third amputation, emphasizing rehabilitation and continuity with prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim,

(the narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who stole, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘They came with a man who had stolen, to Ali<sup>asws</sup> during his<sup>asws</sup> era. So he<sup>asws</sup> cut his hand. They came with him for a second time, so he<sup>asws</sup> cut his opposite leg (left leg). Then they came with him for a third time, so he<sup>asws</sup> imprisoned him for life, and spent upon him from the public treasury of the Muslims and said: ‘This is what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to do. I<sup>asws</sup> will not oppose him<sup>saww</sup>’.
